title: Titan Company FY24: Interrogating the Jewellery Growth Story
scenario: You're covering Titan Company for a Mumbai equity desk. The stock rallied 18% post-results on headline PAT growth of 32%. Your PM wants you to interrogate the income statement: is the profit growth real (operating), or is it padded with one-off gains and tax effects? Run the eight-question checklist.
instructions: Read the Titan FY24 Income Statement, hover tooltips to understand line-item quality, then answer analytical questions decomposing the profit growth into its real sources.
learning_objective: Decompose PAT growth into operating (EBIT) vs non-recurring sources, and grade the quality of each income statement line using the eight-question analyst checklist.
hints: Start by comparing EBIT growth to PAT growth — if they diverge sharply, something below the operating line did the work.
Break the ₹1,248 cr PAT into its five sources: EBIT growth, interest, other income, exceptional items, and tax. Which moved most?
The eight questions matter most for gross margin (direction and why) and the 'other expenses' bucket (what's hiding there). Check the tooltips.

sections.title: Tax & Net Profit — FY24 vs FY23

interactive_highlights.tooltip: Operating revenue grew 25.4% YoY — strong jewellery demand, especially from bridal and festive. But check: was this volume-led (units sold) or price-led (realisation per unit)? Concall will clarify durability.

COGS as % of revenue: FY24 = 59.4%, FY23 = 61.5%. Gross margin *expanded* 210 bps YoY — gold prices were softer, and Titan's product mix shifted toward higher-margin studded jewellery. This is *high-quality* margin expansion.

Other income jumped from ₹423 cr to ₹876 cr (+107%) — this is NOT operating revenue. It's treasury interest (Titan's growing cash), dividend income, and possibly asset-sale gains. Critical: this boost to PBT is *low quality* — it won't recur if cash is deployed.
₹412 cr exceptional gain in FY24 (nil in FY23) — likely a one-time property sale or brand revaluation. This is a *non-recurring* profit booster. Strip it when thinking about repeat earnings.
Effective tax rate fell from 21.8% to 18.4% (340 bps) — this lower rate partly reflects the exceptional gain receiving favourable tax treatment. Tax benefit is *low quality* if it doesn't repeat.

tasks.question: What was the YoY growth in Revenue from operations (%)? Round to 1 decimal place.
tasks.explanation: (31847 - 25403) / 25403 = 25.4%. Strong volume and pricing in jewellery. This is a high-quality headline — now the analyst asks: what % was volume vs price?

tasks.question: EBIT grew from ₹3,744 cr to ₹6,010 cr. What was the YoY growth rate in EBIT (%)? Round to 1 decimal place.
tasks.explanation: (6010 - 3744) / 3744 = 60.4%. EBIT more than doubled — faster than revenue growth (25.4%). This came from margin expansion (gross margin +210 bps, EBITDA margin +390 bps). High-quality operating leverage.

tasks.question: PAT grew 89.8% YoY (from ₹3,016 cr to ₹5,726 cr), but EBIT grew only 60.4%. Which of the following is the BEST explanation for this gap?
tasks.explanation: The 29.4 percentage-point gap (89.8% − 60.4%) came from: (1) Other income jumped 107% (₹453 cr added to PBT), (2) Exceptional gain of ₹412 cr (new to FY24), (3) Tax rate fell 340 bps (saving ₹139 cr). Only the EBIT growth is operating (high quality); the rest are non-recurring or financial (low quality). An analyst would say: 'Underlying operating PAT growth is tracking EBIT (60%+), but the headline 90% includes ₹865 cr of below-the-line boosts.'

tasks.question: Gross margin (COGS as % of revenue) improved by how many basis points from FY23 to FY24?
tasks.explanation: FY24: (31847 - 18912) / 31847 = 40.6%. FY23: (25403 - 15641) / 25403 = 38.5%. Improvement: 210 bps. This reflects softer gold prices and product-mix shift to studded jewellery. High-quality margin expansion — durable if the product mix shift continues.

tasks.question: If you strip the exceptional gain (₹412 cr) and the tax benefit from the lower rate, what is the *adjusted* PAT growth rate (%)? Assume the tax rate had stayed at 21.8%.
tasks.sample_answer: Adjusted PAT = 5726 - 412 (exceptional) - (412 × 0.09) (tax on exceptional) = 5,241 cr. Adjusted tax at 21.8% on PBT ex-exceptional: [(7014 - 412) × 0.218] = 1,444 cr. Adjusted PAT = 6602 - 1444 = 5,158 cr. FY23 PAT was 3,016 cr. Growth = (5158 - 3016) / 3016 = 71.1%. Still strong, but lower than the 89.8% headline. This is the *quality* read.
tasks.explanation: Stripping one-time items and normalising the tax rate reveals the true operating PAT growth is ~71%, not 90%. The headline confuses the reader; the adjusted number tells the analyst the real story. This habit — adjusting for non-recurring items — is how equity research produces credible forecasts.
